english: Maecenas, born from ancestral kings,
note: atavi, strictly great-great-great-grandfathers; Maecenas claimed descent from Etruscan kings.

latin: o et praesidium et dulce decus meum:
english: O both my protection and sweet glory:
note: meum agrees with decus; it is rendered once as 'my' for both nouns.

english: there are those whom in the chariot the Olympic dust
note: curriculo: the racing chariot (some take it as the racecourse).

english: to have gathered pleases, and the turning-post by glowing
note: meta: the turning-post at the end of the course; fervidis: hot from the speed.

english: wheels avoided, and the ennobling palm
note: nobilis taken with palma as 'noble, ennobling'; the palm branch is the victor's prize.

english: raises, lords of the lands, to the gods;
note: terrarum dominos is ambiguous: the victors raised up as lords of the earth, or the gods, who are lords of the earth.

english: this man, if a crowd of fickle Quirites
note: Quirites: the Roman citizens in their civil capacity.

english: strives to raise with triple honours,
note: tergeminis honoribus: the three magistracies of the political career (aedile, praetor, consul).

english: that man, if he has stored in his own granary
whatever is swept from Libyan threshing-floors.
One rejoicing to split with the hoe his ancestral
fields, with Attalic terms
note: Attalicis condicionibus: on terms such as King Attalus of Pergamum (proverbially rich) could offer.

english: you would never move away, so that with a Cyprian beam
note: demoveas: potential subjunctive. trabe: a beam, i.e. a ship's timber, a ship.

english: the Myrtoan, a fearful sailor, he should cut sea.
note: Myrtoum mare: the sea south of Euboea and east of the Peloponnese.

english: Africus wrestling with the Icarian waves
note: Africus: the south-west wind. Icarian: the sea around Icaria.

english: the merchant, fearing, leisure and of the town
note: the merchant praises the leisure and the countryside of his own town; sui (his own) stands on line 17.

latin: laudat rura sui; mox reficit rates
english: praises the countryside, of his own; soon he repairs his boats
note: sui agrees with oppidi on the line above. rates: lit. rafts, i.e. ships; 'his' supplied.

english: shattered, unteachable to endure poverty.

latin: est qui nec veteris pocula Massici
english: There is one who neither cups of old Massic
note: Massic: wine from Mount Massicus in Campania.

latin: nec partem solido demere de die
english: nor a part from the solid day to take away
note: solido de die: from the whole (working) day.

latin: spernit, nunc viridi membra sub arbuto
english: scorns, now under the green arbutus his limbs
note: 'his' supplied.

latin: stratus, nunc ad aquae lene caput sacrae.
english: stretched out, now by the gentle head of a sacred water.
note: caput aquae: the source (head) of a stream; springs were sacred.

latin: multos castra iuvant et lituo tubae
english: Many the camps delight, and, with the lituus, of the trumpet
note: lituus: the curved cavalry horn; tuba: the straight trumpet; tubae goes with sonitus on line 24.

english: the mingled sound, and wars by mothers
detested. There stays under cold Jupiter
note: sub Iove frigido: under the cold sky; Jupiter as the sky.

english: the hunter, of his tender wife unmindful,

latin: seu visa est catulis cerva fidelibus
english: whether a hind has been seen by the faithful hounds
note: catulis: lit. puppies, young hounds.

latin: seu rupit teretes Marsus aper plagas.
english: or a Marsian boar has broken the well-twisted nets.
note: Marsian: from the Marsi in the central Apennines. teretes: rounded, smooth (finely twisted).

english: Me the ivies, rewards of learned brows,
note: hederae is plural; ivy wreaths were the poet's prize.

latin: dis miscent superis, me gelidum nemus
english: mingle with the gods above, me the cool grove
note: dis miscent superis: (the ivies) join me with the gods.

english: and the light dances of Nymphs with Satyrs
note: chori: dances or dancing bands.

english: separate from the people, if neither the pipes
note: tibiae: the double reed-pipes (aulos).

english: Euterpe holds back, nor Polyhymnia
note: Euterpe, Polyhymnia: Muses.

english: refuses to stretch the Lesbian barbitos.
note: barbiton: the Greek lyre of Alcaeus and Sappho of Lesbos; tendere: to tune (stretch the strings).

english: But if you will insert me among the lyric bards,
note: vates: inspired poets, bards.

english: with lofty head I shall strike the stars.
note: vertice: the crown of the head.

latin: Iam satis terris nivis atque dirae
english: Now enough upon the lands of snow and of dire
hail has the father sent, and with reddening
note: pater: Jupiter.

english: right hand having hurled at the sacred citadels
note: iaculatus: having hurled (bolts) at; arces: the heights of the Capitol.

english: he has terrified the city,
terrified the peoples, lest should return the grievous
age of Pyrrha, who complained of new portents,
note: Pyrrha: wife of Deucalion, survivor of the flood; questae agrees with Pyrrhae.

latin: omne cum Proteus pecus egit altos
english: when Proteus drove all the flock, the high
note: pecus: Proteus' herd of seals.

english: to visit mountains,

latin: piscium et summa genus haesit ulmo,
english: and the race of fishes clung in the top of an elm,
which had been a known seat for doves,
and on the overspread the fearful swam
note: superiecto ... aequore: on the water spread over (the land).

english: water, the deer.
note: aequor: the level surface, i.e. the flood water. dammae: deer, does.

english: We have seen yellow Tiber, with twisted back
note: retortis ... undis: with waves turned back (from the sea toward the city).

english: from the Etruscan shore violently waves,
note: litore Etrusco: from the Etruscan (right) bank or shore; sense disputed.

english: go to throw down the monuments of the king
note: deiectum: supine of purpose. regis: Numa, whose Regia stood by the temple of Vesta.

english: and the temples of Vesta,
note: templa: plural for singular.

english: while to Ilia excessively complaining himself
note: Ilia: mother of Romulus, thrown into the Tiber, whose wife she became.

english: he boasts the avenger, and wandering on the left
note: se ... iactat ultorem: vaunts himself as avenger.

latin: labitur ripa Iove non probante u-
english: glides bank, Jove not approving, the wife-
note: the word uxorius is divided between this line and the next.

english: doting river.
note: uxorius: devoted to his wife (Ilia).

english: will hear that citizens have sharpened the iron,
note: ferrum: iron, i.e. the sword.

english: by which the grievous Persians would better perish,
note: Persae: the Parthians. graves: troublesome, oppressive. perirent: subjunctive (would better have perished).

english: will hear of battles, through the vice of parents
note: vitium: fault, vice (the civil wars).

english: the scanty youth.
note: rara: thinned out.

english: Whom of the gods should the people call, of a falling
note: vocet: deliberative subjunctive. ruentis agrees with imperi on the next line.

english: empire, to the affairs? With what prayer should weary
note: imperi rebus: the dative goes with vocet on line 25; fatigent: deliberative subjunctive.

english: the holy virgins her less hearing
note: virgines sanctae: the Vestal virgins; audientem: (Vesta) less listening to.

english: chants, Vesta?
To whom will give the part of expiating the crime
note: partis: the role, function.

english: Jupiter? At last may you come, we pray,
note: venias: jussive/optative subjunctive.

english: in cloud as to gleaming shoulders clothed,
note: amictus: middle participle with accusative of respect, 'having veiled your gleaming shoulders in cloud'.

english: augur Apollo;
or if you prefer, smiling Erycina,
note: Erycina: Venus of Mount Eryx in Sicily. ridens: laughing, smiling.

latin: quam Iocus circum volat et Cupido;
english: around whom Iocus flies and Cupido;
note: Iocus: Jest personified; Cupido: Desire, Cupid.

english: or if the neglected race and descendants
note: nepotes: grandsons, descendants (the Romans, as Mars' offspring).

english: you look back upon, founder,
note: auctor: Mars, founder of the race.

english: alas, sated with too long a game,
note: ludo: game, sport (war).

english: whom the clamour delights and smooth helmets
note: leves: (long e) smooth, polished.

english: and the fierce, of the Marsian foot-soldier, against the bloodied
note: acer agrees with voltus; cruentum agrees with hostem. Marsi is the transmitted reading; some editors read Mauri (Moorish).

english: face, enemy;
note: in hostem: against the (bloodied) enemy.

english: or if, with changed form, a young man
winged, on earth you imitate, of kindly
note: ales: winged one (Mercury). almae agrees with Maiae.

english: son of Maia, enduring to be called
Caesar's avenger:
note: Caesar: Julius Caesar, avenged by Octavian.

english: late into heaven may you return, and long
note: redeas: optative subjunctive.

english: joyful may you be among the people of Quirinus,
note: intersis: be present among. Quirinus: the deified Romulus.

english: and may not you, at our vices hostile,
note: iniquum: hostile, angered.

english: a swifter breeze
note: ocior: too swift (comparative).

english: carry away; here great triumphs rather,

latin: hic ames dici pater atque princeps
english: here may you love to be called father and chief
note: princeps: first citizen, chief man.

english: and may you not allow the Medes to ride unavenged
note: Medi: the Parthians. inultos: unavenged, i.e. unpunished.

english: with you as leader, Caesar.
note: Caesar: Octavian.

english: So you the goddess powerful over Cyprus,
note: diva potens Cypri: Venus. regat (line 3) governs te.

english: so the brothers of Helen, bright stars,
note: Castor and Pollux, protectors of sailors.

english: and of the winds the father may guide,
note: pater ventorum: Aeolus; regat: optative subjunctive

english: the others being bound, except Iapyx,
note: Iapyx: the north-west wind, favourable for sailing from Brundisium to Greece.

english: ship, which, entrusted to you,
note: navis: vocative. quae ... debes: you who owe.

english: owe Vergilius; to the Attic borders
note: Vergilium: the poet Virgil; name kept in its Latin form.

english: may you return him unharmed, I pray,
note: reddas: subjunctive; 'him' supplied.

english: and may you preserve the half of my soul.
note: animae dimidium meae: Virgil.

english: For that man oak and triple bronze
note: illi ... erat: dative of possession, 'that man had'.

latin: circa pectus erat, qui fragilem truci
english: around the breast was, who the fragile to the savage
note: fragilem agrees with ratem; truci with pelago.

english: committed sea raft
note: ratem: raft, boat.

english: first: nor did he fear the headlong Africus
note: Africus: the south-west wind.

english: contending with the Aquilones,
note: Aquilones: north winds.

latin: nec tristis Hyadas nec rabiem Noti,
english: nor the gloomy Hyades nor the rage of Notus,
note: Hyades: rain-bringing star cluster. Notus: the south wind.

english: than whom no arbiter of Hadria
note: quo: than whom (Notus). Hadria: the Adriatic.

latin: maior, tollere seu ponere volt freta;
english: greater, whether to raise or to lay he wishes the straits;
note: freta: straits, seas.

english: what step of death did he fear
note: gradum: step, approach.

english: who with dry eyes the swimming monsters,
who saw the turbid sea and
the ill-famed rocks Acroceraunia?
note: Acroceraunia: the 'thunder-peaks' headland of Epirus.

english: In vain a god cut off,
note: abscidit: cut off, separated.

english: prudent, by the dissociable ocean
note: dissociabili: here active, 'separating'.

english: the lands, if nevertheless impious
note: inpiae agrees with rates on the next line.

english: rafts leap across shallows not to be touched.
note: vada: shallows, waters.

english: Bold to endure all things

latin: gens humana ruit per vetitum nefas:
english: the human race rushes through forbidden wrong:
note: nefas: impiety, what is unlawful before the gods.

english: bold, the offspring of Iapetus
note: Prometheus.

english: fire by evil fraud to the peoples brought;
after fire from the heavenly home
note: aetheria domo: from the home in the upper air.

english: stolen, wasting and a new of fevers
note: nova agrees with cohors on the next line.

english: cohort settled upon the lands
note: incubuit: lay upon, brooded over.

english: and of the formerly remote, slow necessity
note: semoti agrees with Leti on the next line.

english: of Death hastened the step;
note: Leti: genitive with necessitas on line 32; corripuit gradum: hastened its pace.

english: Daedalus tried the empty air
note: expertus (est): perfect of a deponent verb.

english: with wings not given to man;
Herculean labour burst through Acheron.
note: Acheron: river of the underworld.

english: Nothing for mortals is steep:
note: nil ardui: nothing of the steep, nothing arduous.

english: heaven itself we seek in folly, nor
through our crime do we allow
Jupiter to lay down the wrathful thunderbolts.

latin: Solvitur acris hiems grata vice veris et Favoni
english: Sharp winter is loosened by the welcome change of spring and of Favonius
note: Favonius: the west wind of spring.

english: and the machines draw the dry keels,
note: machinae: rollers or winches hauling ships back to the sea.

latin: ac neque iam stabulis gaudet pecus aut arator igni
english: and neither now in the stalls does the herd rejoice nor the ploughman in the fire
nor are the meadows white with hoary frosts.
note: canis pruinis: with white frosts.

latin: iam Cytherea choros ducit Venus imminente luna
english: Now Cytherean Venus leads the dances, with the moon overhanging,
note: Cytherea: of Cythera, Venus' island.

english: and joined to the Nymphs the comely Graces

latin: alterno terram quatiunt pede, dum gravis Cyclopum
english: with alternate foot strike the earth, while the heavy, of the Cyclopes,
note: gravis agrees with officinas on the next line.

english: Volcanus, burning, visits the workshops.
note: Volcanus: Vulcan; ardens: glowing (at his forge).

latin: nunc decet aut viridi nitidum caput impedire myrto
english: now it is fitting either with green myrtle to bind the gleaming head
note: nitidum: shining with oil.

latin: aut flore, terrae quem ferunt solutae,
english: or with flower, which the loosened lands bear,

latin: nunc et in umbrosis Fauno decet immolare lucis,
english: now also in shady groves to Faunus it is fitting to sacrifice,

latin: seu poscat agna sive malit haedo.
english: whether he should demand with a lamb or prefer with a kid.
note: agna, haedo: ablatives of the victim, 'a sacrifice with a ewe-lamb ... with a kid'.

latin: pallida Mors aequo pulsat pede pauperum tabernas
english: Pale Death knocks with impartial foot at the huts of the poor
note: tabernas: booths, hovels.

english: and the towers of kings. O blessed Sestius,
note: beate: fortunate, rich.

latin: vitae summa brevis spem nos vetat inchoare longam;
english: life's brief sum forbids us to begin a long hope;

latin: iam te premet nox fabulaeque Manes
english: soon will press upon you night and the Manes, tales,
note: fabulae: nominative plural in apposition, the Manes mere tales. Manes: the spirits of the dead.

latin: et domus exilis Plutonia; quo simul mearis,
english: and the meagre Plutonian house; where, as soon as you have gone,
note: exilis: thin, meagre.

english: neither the kingdoms of wine will you obtain by lot with knucklebones
note: regna vini: the role of master of the drinking; tali: knucklebones used as dice.

latin: nec tenerum Lycidan mirabere, quo calet iuventus
english: nor tender Lycidas will you marvel at, by whom is warm the youth
note: quo calet: is hot (with love) because of whom.

latin: nunc omnis et mox virgines tepebunt.
english: now all, and soon the maidens will grow warm.

latin: Quis multa gracilis te puer in rosa
english: What slender boy, among much rose, you
note: multa ... in rosa: on many roses, a bed of roses.

english: drenched with liquid perfumes presses
note: urget: presses, courts.

english: in a pleasant, Pyrrha, beneath grotto?
note: grato agrees with antro.

english: For whom do you tie back your yellow hair,
note: 'your' supplied.

english: simple in your elegance? Alas, how often faith
note: simplex munditiis: plain in (your) neatness; 'your' supplied.

english: and changed gods will he weep for, and the rough
note: aspera agrees with aequora on the next line.

english: with black winds seas
note: aequora: level waters, seas (the metaphor of the lover's voyage).

english: will he wonder at, unaccustomed,
note: insolens: unused to it.

latin: qui nunc te fruitur credulus aurea,
english: who now enjoys you, credulous, golden,
note: aurea: (you) golden, agreeing with te.

english: who always free, always lovable
note: vacuam: free (of other attachments), available.

english: hopes you, unaware of the breeze
note: 'you' supplied for the object of sperat.

english: deceitful. Wretched those, for whom
untried you shine. Me, by a tablet, the sacred
note: the metaphor: the shipwrecked lover dedicates his clothes in thanks for escape.

english: votive wall shows, dripping,
note: uvida agrees with vestimenta on line 16.

english: to have hung up to the powerful
garments, of the sea god.
note: potenti maris deo: to the god powerful over the sea; some editors conjecture deae (Venus).

english: You will be written by Varius, brave and of the enemy
note: Varius: L. Varius Rufus, epic and tragic poet.

english: the conqueror, a bird of Maeonian song,
note: alite: in apposition to Vario; Varius as swan of Homeric (Maeonian) song.

latin: quam rem cumque ferox navibus aut equis
english: whatever deed, fierce, on ships or horses
note: quam rem cumque: whatever thing (tmesis).

english: the soldier with you as leader shall have done.
note: gesserit: future perfect (or perfect subjunctive).

latin: nos, Agrippa, neque haec dicere nec gravem
english: We, Agrippa, neither these things to tell nor the heavy
stomach of Pelides, not knowing how to yield,
note: stomachum: bile, wrath. Pelides: Achilles, son of Peleus.

latin: nec cursus duplicis per mare Ulixei
english: nor the courses of double Ulixes through the sea
note: duplicis: double, two-faced, crafty. Ulixes: Odysseus.

english: nor the savage house of Pelops
attempt, slight ones, grand things, while shame
note: tenues grandia: we, slight, (attempting) great themes.

english: and of the unwarlike lyre the powerful Muse forbids
note: Musa potens: the Muse who rules (the lyre).

english: the praises of illustrious Caesar and yours
by fault of talent to wear down.
note: ingeni: of (my) talent; deterere: to diminish.

english: Who Mars covered in an adamantine tunic
note: tunica adamantina: breastplate of adamant.

english: worthily could write of, or with Trojan dust
note: scripserit: potential subjunctive.

english: black Meriones, or by the aid of Pallas
note: Meriones: Cretan hero of the Iliad.

english: Tydides equal to the gods above?
note: Tydides: Diomedes, son of Tydeus.

english: We banquets, we the battles of maidens
with pared nails against young men, fierce ones,
note: acrium agrees with virginum.

english: sing, whether free, or if at all we are burned,
note: vacui: free of love; urimur: we burn (with love).

english: not beyond the usual, light.
note: leves: light, frivolous.

latin: Laudabunt alii claram Rhodon aut Mytilenen
english: Others will praise bright Rhodos or Mytilene
note: place names kept in their Latin (Greek) forms throughout this ode.

english: or Ephesos or of two-sea'd Corinthus
note: bimaris: lying on two seas.

latin: moenia vel Baccho Thebas vel Apolline Delphos
english: the walls, or by Bacchus Thebae or by Apollo Delphi
note: Thebas, Delphos governed by insignis on the next line.

english: distinguished, or Thessalian Tempe;

latin: sunt quibus unum opus est intactae Palladis urbem
english: there are those whose one task is the city of untouched Pallas
note: intactae: virgin. Pallas' city: Athens.

english: with continuous song to celebrate and
note: carmine perpetuo: with an unbroken poem.

english: from everywhere plucked to set before the brow the olive;
note: i.e. to gather olive (Athena's tree) from every source for a garland.

english: very many a one, in honour of Iuno,
note: plurimus: many a man.

latin: aptum dicet equis Argos ditisque Mycenas:
english: will tell of Argos fit for horses and rich Mycenae:
note: dicet: will speak of, sing.

english: me neither so much enduring Lacedaemon
note: patiens: hardy, enduring (Sparta).

latin: nec tam Larisae percussit campus opimae
english: nor so much the plain of rich Larisa has struck
note: percussit: has struck, impressed.

english: as the house of echoing Albunea
note: Albunea: a Sibyl and her spring at Tibur.

latin: et praeceps Anio ac Tiburni lucus et uda
english: and headlong Anio and the grove of Tiburnus and wet
note: Tiburnus: founder of Tibur. uda agrees with pomaria.

english: with moving streams the orchards.

latin: albus ut obscuro deterget nubila caelo
english: As white, from a dark sky, wipes away clouds
note: albus: bright, clearing.

english: often Notus and does not give birth to rains
note: Notus: the south wind.

latin: perpetuos, sic tu sapiens finire memento
english: perpetual, so you, wise, remember to end
note: memento: future imperative.

english: sadness and the labours of life

latin: molli, Plance, mero, seu te fulgentia signis
english: with mellow, Plancus, unmixed wine, whether you, gleaming with standards,
note: fulgentia agrees with castra. merum: wine not mixed with water.

english: the camp holds, or the dense will hold
note: densa agrees with umbra.

latin: Tiburis umbra tui. Teucer Salamina patremque
english: shade of your Tibur. Teucer, Salamis and father
note: Teucer, son of Telamon, banished from Salamis by his father.

english: when he was fleeing, nevertheless, wet with Lyaeus,
note: Lyaeus: Bacchus, i.e. wine. uda agrees with tempora.

english: temples with a poplar garland is said to have bound,
note: the poplar was sacred to Hercules, patron of travellers.

english: thus having addressed his sad friends:
note: tristis: accusative plural with amicos; 'his' supplied.

latin: “quo nos cumque feret melior fortuna parente,
english: “Wherever us will carry a fortune better than a parent,
note: quotation marks as in the Latin source. quo ... cumque: tmesis.

english: we shall go, O allies and companions,

latin: nil desperandum Teucro duce et auspice Teucro:
english: nothing is to be despaired with Teucer as leader and Teucer as auspex:
note: auspice Teucro: under Teucer's auspices.

english: for unerring Apollo has promised
note: certus: sure, reliable.

english: that an ambiguous Salamis on new land would be.
note: ambiguam: a second Salamis (in Cyprus) to be confused with the first.

english: O brave and having suffered worse things

latin: mecum saepe viri, nunc vino pellite curas;
english: with me often, men, now with wine drive away cares;
tomorrow the huge sea we shall travel again.”
note: iterabimus: we shall repeat (the voyage over). Quotation marks as in the source.

english: Lydia, tell, by all

latin: te deos oro, Sybarin cur properes amando
english: the gods you I beg, why Sybaris you hasten by loving
note: the indirect-question subjunctives (properes, oderit, equitet, temperet) are rendered with English present, as English requires.

english: to destroy, why the sunny

latin: oderit campum patiens pulveris atque solis,
english: he hates field, enduring of dust and of sun,
note: campum: the Campus Martius, the exercise ground.

english: why neither soldierly
note: militaris agrees with aequalis.

latin: inter aequalis equitet, Gallica nec lupatis
english: among peers he rides, nor Gallic with wolf-toothed
note: lupatis: jagged bits. Gallica: Gallic (horses').

english: controls mouths bits?
note: frenis: with bits, bridles.

latin: cur timet flavum Tiberim tangere? cur olivum
english: why does he fear to touch yellow Tiber? why olive-oil
note: olivum: olive oil, used by wrestlers.

english: than viper's blood

latin: cautius vitat neque iam livida gestat armis
english: more cautiously avoids, nor now bruised does he carry from weapons
note: livida: livid, black and blue; armis: from (handling) weapons.

english: arms, often by the discus,
note: bracchia: arms (limbs).

latin: saepe trans finem iaculo nobilis expedito?
english: often beyond the mark, famed, the javelin sent off?
note: iaculo nobilis expedito: famous for the javelin thrown.

english: Why does he lie hidden, as of marine
note: marinae agrees with Thetidis.

latin: filium dicunt Thetidis sub lacrimosa Troiae
english: the son, they say, of Thetis, under the tearful of Troy
note: sub ... funera: on the eve of, near the time of; lacrimosa agrees with funera. Achilles hid in women's dress on Scyros.

english: deaths, lest manly
note: funera: deaths, funerals.

latin: cultus in caedem et Lycias proriperet catervas?
english: dress into slaughter and the Lycian bands should snatch forth?
note: cultus: dress, attire; proriperet: hurry (him) forth; 'him' implied.
